title: Milton Larkin's band at the Rum Boogie in Chicago
summary: In 1942 Larkin's band goes to Joe Louis's Rum Boogie in Chicago, six men short because of the draft, and stays nine months with Cobb there five.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: And this was during the war days. See, I left in '42 with Milton Larkin, going to Chicago, in Joe Louis' Rum Boogie there.

We went in for a month with a month option, and the band was so great until they picked up the month option. Tiny Bradshaw was to come in -- Charlie Fokes, a baritone saxophone player who is with Basie now, has got a kitchenette, getting ready to set up to cook, while they're going to be there for a month ... and it didn't work out that way, because we were doing too much business. They had them roped off in front. The band from Texas -- we had a Texas map, and during that time the song, "Deep in the Heart of Texas" was popular, and Cedrick made arrangements for this song, "Deep in the Heart of Texas", and that's what we had on our bandstand in the map of Texas ... Deep from the Heart of Texas, and we liked to set that joint on fire. T-Bone was on that show. Joe Ziggle Johnson had the coast girls operating. You listen to what I say. There was five, but we went in six men short, and
we had to get Chicago musicians to fill their spot.
Why did you go in six men short?
That's how, with Greetings. "Greetings now-- I want you with me."

Well, what were we gonna do? But we went in and got six Chicago musicians and that put us in. Politics. and Now, we didn't know that. But when Tiny Bradshaw came in, his contract didn't mean nothing. Took it down to Harry Grave's office, who was the President of the union, and it didn't mean nothing and just tear it up. That's what he told Charlie Graham, who was running the Rum Boogie.
Milton Larkin's band stayed at the Rum Boogie 9 months. I stayed five of the nine and joined him.
